dialogues.text: Good morning, Dash! Got any plans today?
Good morning, Whizzy! I do, I plan to lock in at the CLIR.
(Whizzy looks confused) Lock in?
It means to focus on something. In this case, I'll be locking in at the CLIR for the upcoming exams.
Ohh! Yes, I understand it now. That's new to me! Well then, I'll also be locking in on studying the arts of Wizardry. See you and good luck, Dash!
Thanks Whizzy, you too!
Hello again, Dash! I'm here to talk about Sustainable Development Goal #4: Quality Education!
Hi Whizzy! What is SDG 4 all about?
SDG 4 focuses on ensuring an inclusive and equitable quality education and promoting lifelong learning opportunities for everyone.
As students, you can contribute to this goal by donating used books, promoting and taking free online courses, mentoring young people, and participating in school supply drives, to name a few.
If you would like more information, you can check out the official Global Goals' webpage on this goal!
Hello again, Dash! I'm here to talk about Sustainable Development Goal #13: Climate Action!
Hi Whizzy! What is SDG 13 all about?
SDG 13 focuses on combating climate change by reducing emissions, enhancing resilience, and promoting climate policies globally.
As students, you can help by conserving energy, reducing waste, using eco-friendly transportation, spreading awareness, and supporting climate initiatives, to name a few.
If you would like more information, you can check out the official Global Goals' webpage on this goal!
(Laura talks to herself) Hmm, what should I do with all this?
Hi Laura! What are those?

Oh, hi Dash! Yes, these are some leftover props from the stage play but no one claimed them. I’m thinking of organizing them based on whether the prop item can be segregated, recycled, or has to be thrown away.
Why not just throw everything away?
That’ll only end up harming our environment if you don’t properly dispose of your waste items. Besides, doing this helps you practice SDG 13 as well as reducing the impact of climate change!
That makes sense. Let's segregate them!
All right! I'll segregate them, but if I put it in the wrong bin, I'd like you to tell me.
Hi again! Thanks for helping me. I got the hang of it now!
Do you want to learn more about SDG 13: Climate Action?
Eight... ten... twelve Filipino books...
Good day Gab! What's going on?
Hey, Dash! We’re currently doing a book drive in support of SDG 4 Quality Education. Would you like to donate?
Really? Great! What is it?
Woah, Magic 101? Thanks for your contribution! Would love to read it while I'm here. I won't bring it home, of course!
No problem!
That’s okay. The book drive will run until Friday, then we’ll deliver them by next week.
Oh, awesome!
Speaking of donations, I was going to collect some books on this floor, but then no one would be here in case someone wants to donate here directly…
I can help!
Really? You’ll do that? Thank you! You just need to visit R308, R306, R304, and R302 for the books they donated.
The rooms are on the right.
Hey! You're back with the books! Took you a while.
Yeah! I was suddenly tested on my ICT, STEM, ABM, and HUMSS knowledge. It was...
Really? That's great! I'm sure you'll do great in quiz bees.
Really? Well, you can't learn if you don't make mistakes. You'll get better!
Anyway, thanks for bringing the books! I was able to collect around 20 more books while you were gone. See you, Dash!
Hey! Thanks for helping me. These donations will surely be of help.
Do you want to learn more about SDG 4: Quality Education?

Don’t worry, they won’t be that hard. I have 3 questions in total, but you only need to get one right. You can do it!
Question 1: What variable type stores true or false?
Close! It's boolean. A boolean's value can either be true or false. A string, on the other hand, stores text values.
Correct! As promised, here are your books! If you'd like, you can come back to answer all my ICT questions to test your knowledge.
Question 2: What tool can you use to create geometric shapes in Adobe Animate?
Close! It's Shape tool. The shape tool is for making simple geometric shapes, while the lasso tool is used for selecting elements.
Question 3: What is the process of constructing a series of bones or a skeleton for your 2D or 3D model?

Close! It's rigging. Rigging is the process of constructing a skeleton that you can easily move to animate your character, while tweening is the process of creating intermediate frames between keyframes to smoothly animate objects!

Question 1: What is the powerhouse of the cell?

Close! It's mitochondria. A mitochondria is called the powerhouse of the cell as it produces energy through cellular respiration. The nucleus, on the other hand, is the control center of the cell as it contains genetic material and regulates cell activities like growth and reproduction.
Correct! As promised, here are your books! If you'd like, you can come back to answer all my STEM questions to test your knowledge.
Question 2: What is the term for the shape of the graph of a quadratic function?
Close! It's parabola. A parabola is the U-shaped curve that is the graph of a quadratic function, while parabula is Filipino for parable, a simple story that tells a moral or lesson.
Question 3: What is the term for the ability of a material to return to its original shape after being stretched or compressed?

Close! It's elasticity. Elasticity is the ability of a material to return to its original shape after being stretched or deformed, while plasticity is the tendency of a material to undergo permanent deformation when a force is applied.

Question 1: The Accounting Equation uses what math operation (Assets = Liabilities ? Equity)?

Close! It's Liabilities + Equity. Assets are what a company owns, Liabilities are what a company owes, and Equity represents the owner's stake in a business, calculated as the difference between the company's assets and liabilities, essentially what's left after all debts are paid.
Correct! As promised, here are your books! If you'd like, you can come back to answer all my ABM questions to test your knowledge.
Question 2: Who is the modern father of accounting?

Close! It's Luca Pacioli. Luca Pacioli was an Italian mathematician who was the first person to comprehensively write about double-entry accounting, while Alan Turing is the father of modern computer science.
Question 3: What do you call a business that purchases products from other businesses like manufacturers and sells them to customers at a higher retail price?

Close! It's called a merchandising business. A merchandising business buys finished goods and resells them to customers, while a manufacturing business produces its own products from raw materials to sell.

Close! It's sociology. Sociology studies human society and group behavior, while psychology focuses on individual mental processes and behavior.
Correct! As promised, here are your books! If you'd like, you can come back to answer all my HUMSS questions to test your knowledge.
Question 2: What is the branch of philosophy that deals with moral principles?

Close! It's ethics. Ethics involves the moral principles that guide individual behavior, distinguishing right from wrong based on societal or personal values, while law refers to a system of rules established by a governing authority to regulate behavior and maintain order.
Question 3: What is the process by which individuals or groups adopt the cultural norms and values of another society?

Close! It's acculturation. Acculturation is the process by which individuals or groups adopt the cultural traits or social patterns of another group, while subculture refers to a smaller cultural group within a larger society that has distinct values, norms, and lifestyles.
